firmwares.about: A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.
firmwares.name: AMB-1

firmwares.about: A live jungle tool built around classic breaks (Amen, Apache, Think) and your own. Hold white keys for rolls, builds, echo and Akai-style metallic stretch, play hits on the black keys, and shape the break with variation, warp, ringing feedback, lo-fi, EQ, saturation and compression.
firmwares.name: AMENITY

firmwares.about: Arctic Scream is a dark-ambient drone machine built on GR!MM: four tracks over FM, supersaw, formant, tonewheel, physical-model, phase-distortion and sample sources, plus Holvut, a feedback string-and-body loop that wakes, howls and overblows into screams. Drones wander and build like a storm; WARP and MORPH twist the sound, with a huge SPACE reverb and freeze, GRAIN, TAPE and a HORROR scale.
firmwares.name: Arctic Scream p0larpatch

firmwares.about: Epic film sounds: an eight-voice spectral pad of sine partials that drifts on its own, a swarm of saws, shaped wind, a shimmer plate, a tape delay and a freeze that holds a cloud of grains. Every page is a picture the four knobs shift, and HOME is an aurora bent by the sound.
firmwares.name: AURORA

firmwares.about: A generative Berlin School MIDI sequencer: a small ensemble of voices that repeat, phase against each other on loops of unequal length and earn their mutations over time. The FM-1 makes no sound with it: each voice goes out over USB on its own MIDI channel to your synths, as Berlinan for macOS…
firmwares.name: Berlinan

firmwares.about: A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.
firmwares.name: Bytemania

firmwares.about: Multi-engine synth firmware with DRONE, STASIS texture capture, Pair Morph, and per-track Random Morph and Morph Journey for evolving, ambient and experimental sound design. Sequencer, MIDI Learn, USB audio.
firmwares.name: Caravel

firmwares.about: CARNAC OS is a dual-timbral wavetable synth inspired by neolithic monuments and forgotten rituals. Built for deep sound design and immediate control, with a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer and a J6-style chord arp. The PCM waves need a separate installer: get it from my GitHub page.
firmwares.name: Carnac OS

firmwares.about: A ultra-refined Chiptune music editor, featuring over 35 classic chips such as NES, Gameboy, heck even the Sunsoft 5B! Gimmick fans rejoice!
firmwares.name: Chipbox

firmwares.about: A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.
firmwares.name: ChoralRoot

firmwares.about: A pocket symphony orchestra groovebox with strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion. Compose in piano roll or musical notation, conduct individual sections with articulations, dynamics and expression curves, and arrange patterns into complete pieces.
firmwares.name: CONDUCTOR

firmwares.about: Chords after the Orchid, with controls made for the FM-1: one key plays a chord with a bass note. Also 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a sequencer with drums and a song mode, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.
firmwares.name: CoralFlower

firmwares.about: CTL-1 turns the FM-1 into a MIDI controller: keys with velocity and aftertouch in any scale with chords under the black keys, four knobs sending controllers in four banks, an arpeggiator and a four-track Euclidean drum sequencer on its clock. Everything goes out as MIDI, and the built-in General MIDI sounds play along, so it works with nothing connected.
firmwares.name: CTL-1

firmwares.about: An Elektron-style six-track groovebox for the FM-1, with Elektron Syntakt support. One-press quick-start loops, generators for acid lines, dub chords, held atmospheres and modular bleeps, trig conditions and locks, a DJ filter and FX pad, and the keys set the song's key. Built on JIANT FM.
firmwares.name: cursed os

firmwares.about: An Arabic wedding keyboard. Maqam scales with quarter tones on any note, dabke and shaabi rhythms, mijwiz, zurna, oud and qanun voices, a drone, eight tracks with loops and steps. Lean on a key and the note bends. An Akai MIDImix works as its mixer.
firmwares.name: DABKE

firmwares.about: An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.
firmwares.name: DRIFT

firmwares.about: Microtonic, for the FM-1! Roll the dice for a kit, build one from scratch, or bring in your Microtonic presets and patterns. Share kits and patterns as files, and send it all to your Teenage Engineering PO-32! Built on Chipbox!
firmwares.name: Drumlab

firmwares.about: A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.
firmwares.name: DUB-1

firmwares.about: In dub, the mixing desk is the instrument. Dubwise FM is an eight-channel reggae band (FM drums, bass, skank, organ, melodica or horns, sirens and shouts), each channel with a mute and a throw, feeding a tape echo you can push into feedback and a spring reverb you can kick. Quantised mutes land on the one with a countdown, the stepped Big Knob filter clicks like King Tubby's, and every drop, throw and sweep is yours: nothing plays itself. Record your moves into a song, recall them as scenes, or take the eight stems out over USB.
firmwares.name: DUBWISE
firmwares.tag: A dub mixing desk you play live

firmwares.about: A MULTIMORPHING bitimbral synth: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound. Ten engines including wavetables, twin filters, effects and a mod matrix. Layer, dual or stereo mode. Velocity sensitivity and aftertouch. Dual core.
firmwares.name: DUELL (unofficial build)

firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox that is a dungeon crawler: your party plays the music, the rogue drums, the fighter bass, the cleric pads and the mage the melody. Step-program in a tracker or record live, and see how deep you get.
firmwares.name: Dungeon Tracker

firmwares.about: A granular sampler: a few seconds of any sound become slow clouds, sparkles, tape loops and swells, played from the keys and knobs. Six modes (CLOUD, DUST, TAPE, BLOOM, PULSE, DRIFT), held performance effects, RANDOM with locks, RESAMPLE, 14 CC0 factory sounds and 16 slots for your own, with a companion web app for samples and presets.
firmwares.name: ECHOFIELD

firmwares.about: Draw your own waveforms, morph between sounds, and bring them to life with modulation, evolving textures, and powerful effects. From warm analog-inspired tones to wild experimental soundscapes, ETCH puts sound design right at your fingertips.
firmwares.name: ETCH

firmwares.about: The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.
firmwares.name: Felucca

firmwares.about: A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.
firmwares.name: FiMba-1

firmwares.about: A groovebox around one engine, ChoralRoot's FM TONE: eight tracks, p-locks and preset sound locks, conditions, ratchets, chords, and MIDI FX for generative patterns and for reworking the ones you have. Bluetooth MIDI, and recording over USB audio.
firmwares.license: MPL-2.0 AND GPL-3.0-only AND MIT AND FTL AND OFL-1.1
firmwares.name: FIZZ

firmwares.about: A singing human voice for the FM-1, ported from Jameson Hodge's CHIMERA. A simulated airway (lungs, vocal folds, throat, mouth, nose) sings words a syllable per key, or holds vowels you shape with the knobs. Write the words in the browser Studio and send them over USB.
firmwares.name: FM-1 Chimera Vocal

firmwares.about: C64 music on the FM-1: a 6510 runs each tune's own code and reSID plays it, PSID and RSID. A GoatTracker 2 editor on the FM-1 itself with ten GT2 example songs, a SID synth with a sequencer and effects, and any .sid sent from the browser plays at once.
firmwares.name: FM-1 SID

firmwares.about: A kick drum synthesizer with a sequencer of up to 32 steps: seven kinds of kick and 48 parameters, p-locks of any parameter on any step, step conditions and chance, nine generators, four LFOs, live and final effects with a hall reverb, three pattern banks, four projects and six themes.
firmwares.name: FM-KICK

firmwares.about: A Mega Drive / Genesis music tracker. It emulates the YM2612 and SN76489 chips: six FM channels, three square waves and noise, with Deflemask-style effects, 128 FM presets, a drum kit on the DAC, 256 song slots, a demo song and VGM export.
firmwares.name: FM1-TRAX

firmwares.about: A semi-modular mono synth calibrated knob by knob on a real one: VCO, self-oscillating 4-pole ladder filter, LFO, ADSR, VCA, wave folder, S+H, mixer and a patchbay with normals and dummy plugs. Four tracks, MIDI clock sync, chorus, delay and reverb, 90 sounds.
firmwares.name: FMav-1

firmwares.about: A three-oscillator monosynth in the spirit of the classic Moogs: a 24 dB/octave ladder filter, two contours, 100 factory patches, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and MIDI. Built on Felucca.
firmwares.name: FMini-1

firmwares.about: A throaty talking formant synth with a 303-style sequencer: a saw wave through a three-formant vowel filter, resonant low-pass, drive and ping-pong delay. 16 steps with vowels, accent and slide, a pattern randomizer, 16 stored patterns, Bluetooth MIDI and tight clock sync.
firmwares.name: FMLARYNX

firmwares.about: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.
firmwares.name: FoMni-1

firmwares.about: Dungeon synth: a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.
firmwares.name: GHOULBOX

firmwares.about: One analog-style synth laid out like the classic microKORG, with a screen that draws the sound.
firmwares.name: Golana

firmwares.about: A wavetable synthesizer: two oscillators that morph through 130 wavetables, with unison and warps, a ladder filter, a modulation matrix and effects. Its 32-step sequencer can move the wavetable and the filter on every step.
firmwares.name: Golf

firmwares.about: Neon-noir groovebox firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: four tracks, seven sources, tape and megacity space FX, sixteen scales (Insen, Hirajoshi, Iwato, whole tone), and forty-four Blade Runner factory sounds. Its screen: a glitched landscape that tears with the sound.
firmwares.name: GR!MM

firmwares.about: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream firmware: 4 tracks, 7 sound sources, real recorded choirs, tracks that play by themselves, and long tape, granular and reverb effects.
firmwares.name: GR!MM

firmwares.about: A chord and string instrument: 16 synthesized sounds, 50 chord styles, editable voicings, guitar tunings, and Freeplay, Strum and Arp modes with partial-chord pulses.
firmwares.name: GuitChordi

firmwares.about: Generative dark ambient: drones, demonic and angelic choirs, bells and 135 sound effects that keep changing by themselves across 15 worlds, with 40 melting pictures. Play bells or latch choir voices on the keys, or play and hold effects. Works on older and newer FM-1s (both flash chips).
firmwares.name: HADAL-1

firmwares.about: Noise and modeling synth with GM-style presets (4 banks, 512) and a 4-track tape recorder: each voice a live Chua circuit or noise program, through vactrol gates into resonators and piano, drum, voice, flute, brass, bowed, reed and bird waveguides, with temple, cathedral and mosque reverbs. XG…
firmwares.name: HAWK CHUA

firmwares.about: A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects. Play it in the browser first.
firmwares.name: Hortator

firmwares.about: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1. One of a pack of four: LOF-1 (a lofi groovebox), ECO-1 (a plant plays it) and GRAV-1 (a star and its planets), experimental, on its project page.
firmwares.name: HYP-1

firmwares.about: A groovebox for the FM-1 with three synth tracks, four drum lanes, 24 Plaits engines, 128 starting sounds, a pattern arranger and a 64-step sequencer. Shape your mix with track effects, shared reverb and master controls.
firmwares.name: JamesOS

firmwares.about: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.
firmwares.name: JIANT FM

firmwares.about: K-WA SUB is a powerful bass synthesizer for the M-VAVE FM-1, featuring 9 synthesis engines with 2 engines playable simultaneously and morphing capabilities. A dedicated sample layer adds attack and texture, while 3 freely assignable MIDI-learnable LFOs, quantized live effects and extensive sound…
firmwares.name: K-WASUB
firmwares.tag: K-WA SUB is a powerful bass…

firmwares.about: Kris Jangle is a Christmas game for the FM-1: it plays the start of a carol and you replay it on the keys, building three notes per level up to the whole song. Four carols, three play modes from guided EASY to sound-only HARD, and Grump Mode on three misses.
firmwares.name: KRIS JANGLE

firmwares.about: Synth2, the open-source recreation of Synth1, on eight voices across both cores: two oscillators and a sub, five filters (LPDL among them), two LFOs, distortions and phasers, EQ, delay, chorus and Synth1's arpeggiator. It plays Synth1's .sy1 patches, with the Synth2 Factory bank built in and 1024…
firmwares.name: M-Vsynth2

firmwares.about: A modular synth you patch in the browser: modules (oscillators, filters, envelopes, delays) nest into assemblies you save and reuse, and the patch plays on the FM-1, polyphonic with a Voicing module.
firmwares.name: Matryoshka

firmwares.about: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.
firmwares.name: Melodee

firmwares.about: Mighty Arp, from the creator of Mighty Synth Sampler, is a 4-op FM/subtractive synth built around a chance arpeggiator. Just hold a chord and let chance play the melody. 50 sounds plus a RANDOM mode that invents new ones, a 32-step sequencer, chords, effects and more.
firmwares.name: Mighty Arp

firmwares.about: Felucca with six tracks and new engines: SID, Braids' 48 models, a TB-303 and engines after Elektron's Analog Four, SY Chip and Digitone 2, a ping-pong delay and a new reverb. Built on Felucca 1.5.
firmwares.name: Mini-Tone

firmwares.about: Six monophonic tracks of synth and FX machines, pages of eight knobs, a filter and a tape delay on every track, three LFOs a track, parameter locks and slides. Forked from Hortator, with sounds ported from MONO2K.
firmwares.name: MNM-1

firmwares.about: A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators modulating each other through eight routings, and keys that move a cursor on an XY pad instead of playing notes: white keys are points, black keys gestures. ARP, a polymetric sequencer, a clock in Hz and eight generative environments.
firmwares.name: MODELAR

firmwares.about: Turns the FM-1 into a steel tongue drum: hold it in both hands, play with your thumbs, and every note falls like a drop into a pond where koi swim.
firmwares.name: Modular Koi

firmwares.about: Six mono machines in the spirit of Elektron's Monomachine: FM, superwaves, wavetables, a SID, a voice and four drum synths, one per track. A 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, a lofi bus, four demo parts and a web patch editor.
firmwares.name: MONO2K

firmwares.about: A sad wavetable synth played by a pixel blob in a rainy room: its eyes are the filter, its mouth the envelope, its tears the delay. Toy-keyboard accompaniment with 13 gloomy beats, auto-bass, arpeggiator, loop recorder.
firmwares.name: MOPE-1

firmwares.about: Learn and use Morse code. Key on the piano keys (straight key or iambic paddles) and see what you sent, drill short and long presses, learn by sound with flash cards, listen to endless practice, type letters and CW phrases on the keys. Keying goes out over USB-MIDI or Bluetooth MIDI in the Vail…
firmwares.name: MORSE

firmwares.about: Six generative tracks, 279 musical Biomes plus Blank, 652 Tones, music-linked Itinera dreams and six USB audio stems. Each track takes any sound while keeping its notes and rhythm.
firmwares.name: Mutable Dreams

firmwares.about: Generative 1970s Berlin School: two sequencers drift against each other over a drone, in eight endless pieces. Play a melody on the white keys and the lead answers it, takes it as its theme and grows new ideas from it.
firmwares.name: NACHTFAHRT

firmwares.about: Two drones that breathe and drift on their own, after the Lyra-8, Subharmonicon and DS-2: twelve presets on the white keys, gestures and scenes to move them, an LFO, delay and a reverb that freezes. Press PLAY to fade them in.
firmwares.name: Niagara Drift

firmwares.about: An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84, now on four tracks: each its own sound, arp and sequence; a mixer with chorus, delay, plate reverb and drive sends, a master with DJ filter and compressor. Tracks start on the bar, patterns keep their sounds.
firmwares.name: OberVave

firmwares.about: A four-voice synthesizer: two oscillators per voice, each STD (8 waves), SUPER (7 detuned saws, squares, triangles or sines), WT or GRAIN; a 12/24 dB multimode filter, two ADSRs, two LFOs, unison, delay, reverb and chorus. 16 factory presets, 16 of yours. Play it in the browser first.
firmwares.name: ObsSynth

firmwares.about: It's an organ. Three manuals with 84 free-running tone generators and no voice stealing, eight models from tonewheel and combo organs to pipe organs and free reeds, drawbars, percussion, rotary, drive, delay and reverb, 16 performance setups, three MIDI zones and Yamaha SEQTRAK control.
firmwares.name: OrGigs

firmwares.about: A modular synth for the FM-1. With over 80 modules, including synth engines, samplers, filters, effects, sequencers, and generative tools, you can build, patch, and perform directly on the hardware.
firmwares.name: PATCHWERK

firmwares.about: A cinematic space drone you travel through, not one that plays itself. Five drone voices hold a pedal; turn PRESET and they glide to the next scene one voice at a time, or MORPH there by hand. Play VOX over it in key, loop it and the loop follows the key, or hold a key to bend and throw the sound.
firmwares.name: Penumbra

firmwares.about: A generative groovebox you perform on: ten genres of self-playing pieces, an auto-DJ with breakdowns, builds and drops, Euclidean drums, an acid line that answers itself, beat FX and DX7-style FM voices from your own .syx.
firmwares.name: PERF-1

firmwares.about: An old-school hip-hop and house sampler after the SP-404 and the PO-33: two song samples and a 16-pad kit, up to 32 chops a song, a 64-step sequencer, patterns and a song arrangement. Built on Felucca.
firmwares.name: PIGEON

firmwares.about: A generative garden pond. Switch it on and it plays itself: breathing voices, water drops, a gliding bass and quiet drips, with echo and reverb. Nine pieces, from a quiet pond to rain and thunder. Pick a piece and a scale, take notes out or put them back, and let it grow.
firmwares.name: POND

firmwares.about: A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.
firmwares.name: PurpleMonkey

firmwares.about: A six-track groovebox for the M-VAVE FM-1: nine engines and 273 sounds (analog, six-operator FM, wavetable, digital drums), a 64-step sequencer with probability and ratchets, song mode, scales and chords, a mod matrix and three FX buses, plus a browser emulator and a web editor.
firmwares.name: Quantum GammaWave

firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox: Plaits' 24 models, a 16-pad kit, a step sequencer with p-locks and trig conditions, eight generative sources (Game of Life, chord progressions, Tonnetz walks, orbits, an improviser that learns from you...), punch-in effects and an animated scene on every page.
firmwares.name: QUARTZ

firmwares.about: An eight-track groovebox for sound design: thirteen synth engines, struck percussion and 33 drum machines after the Machinedrum, on an influence grid where any track can trigger, excite or modulate any other.
firmwares.name: Ravel

firmwares.about: The firmware this site installs, running as itself. On its own (0.3) the FM-1 is a DX7 with Yamaha's ROM voices, a MIDI controller, a looper and an arp; when a computer connects it becomes that computer's panel.
firmwares.name: RemoteFM1

firmwares.about: A monophonic bass synth on Cycle Exchange Synthesis: two sub-oscillators, a ladder filter, Channel EQ, eight effects from MOSFET drive to octave fuzz, a step sequencer up to 128 steps and an arpeggiator.
firmwares.name: RUPTURE

firmwares.about: An 8-voice virtual analog tweak synth: authentic 4-pole resonant filter, dual sub-oscillator, ADSR envelopes, 64-step sequencer, and hands-on live performance controls.
firmwares.name: S1Vave

firmwares.about: A slow generative ambient piece that plays itself for hours and never repeats: a choir pad, soft bells, a gliding bass and a rare low ground drift through harmonies and colours like weather. Four pieces, four knobs to tend it (Mood, Density, Drift, Space). A fork of AMB-1.
authors: Tomorrow's Man, from AMB-1 by Charles Vestal
firmwares.name: SAMSARA

firmwares.about: The Commodore 64's SID chip, twice for six voices. Its web app edits patches and takes them straight from .sid game music files.
firmwares.name: SID-1

firmwares.about: Plays C64 SID music from HVSC on an emulated 6581 or 8580 and lets you remix every voice live: transpose, mute, solo, swap waveforms, bend envelopes and filter, add LFOs, ride the tempo. Out of the jack, as USB audio or over ASID to a real SID. MIDI clock from the tune, or the tune synced to yours.
firmwares.name: SiDJ

firmwares.about: Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs measured on real chips, a GoatTracker 2 tracker and step sequencer with slide and accent, .sid playback, LAB for sounds with tables and LFOs, AI-made songs and sounds, SidStation banks, Bluetooth MIDI and keyboards, Live Link and scene art you draw.
firmwares.name: SIDOU
firmwares.tag: Turns the FM-1 into a C64…

firmwares.about: Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca, with most of Felucca 1.6.1's work brought over (the second core, MIDI LEARN, INSERT); Felucca's sounds and projects load. Also runs on the SMK-37 Pro. Coming from 1.x: 2.0 saves in new formats – update on Skiff's own page (it backs up and converts), or back up in its editor first.
firmwares.name: Skiff

firmwares.about: SLOOP rewritten from scratch: five tracks, 13 sound engines, 153 sounds, 46 drum kits, a step sequencer with a piano roll, 27 punch-in effects, six visualisers and a web editor. A public beta.
firmwares.name: SLOOP 3

firmwares.about: You're making acid, baby! Smash that LFO button until you hear something you like, and then twist those knobs! Now with 100% more FX! A truly trippy experience! Built on Chipbox.
firmwares.name: Smileyface

firmwares.about: The talking synth, its FM-1 build: every key speaks the next word of a sentence at its pitch and chords speak in harmony; nine voices, 20 banks of sentences and songs, RHYTHM with an 808.
firmwares.name: Speak37

firmwares.about: SPELLBOX turns the FM-1 into a talking spelling toy after the 1978 Speak & Spell: an 8-character fluorescent display, a 10-pole LPC voice at 8 kHz through an 8-bit DAC, and the SPELL, LETTER, SAY IT, SECRET CODE and MYSTERY WORD games over four levels, with the keys as an A-to-Z keyboard. SPEAK…
firmwares.name: SPELLBOX

firmwares.about: A synthesizer with 26 engines and 819 level-matched factory sounds: three-oscillator HYBRID, six-operator FM, wavetables, early-1980s polysynths, a semi-modular two-filter voice, physical models and more. One instrument with a modulation matrix, arpeggiator and step sequencer, edited in the browser.
firmwares.name: Stallion

firmwares.about: A Synth1-inspired polysynth that plays two sounds at once in bitimbral mode: layered, split or on two MIDI channels. 256 presets in 13 categories, 1,024 user slots. Two oscillators plus sub, FM, ring mod, sync, four filters, arp, drone and effects. 3,174 more sounds in the Patch Manager.
firmwares.name: SY1

firmwares.about: An instrument for slow, evolving sound. Four layers play recorded sources as drifting loops, grains, time-stretch or resonating strings, mixed by a vector point that moves by itself, with shimmer reverb and freeze.
firmwares.name: Tekstuur

firmwares.about: Makes the FM-1 a small generative modular system. Rather than just generating notes, its thirteen generators create musical relationships: tracks follow, answer and share one harmony, and song forms develop over time. An instrument first, with one musical idea behind it.
firmwares.name: Tessera

firmwares.about: Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.
firmwares.name: Tonitor

firmwares.about: A trap and phonk groovebox: six tracks with 808s, FM keys, bells and pads, generators for drums, hats, chords and bass, a sampler with slices, a piano roll, a live performance page with mutes, effect throws and bar jumps, and tape, VHS and vinyl colour on the master.
firmwares.name: TRAPSTATION OS

firmwares.about: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.
firmwares.name: Vector37

firmwares.about: A four-track tape looper in the spirit of a cassette Portastudio. Record from Bluetooth or USB audio, overdub and punch in, set each track's speed, pitch and pan, bounce through a resonant filterbank, record knob motion, slice loops, and route two LFOs to any knob.
firmwares.name: Viscera

firmwares.about: Ambient as a living window: cherry petals on a river, koi in a pond, fireflies under a real moon, and every movement a note. Set it down and let it play; the keys play along, the knobs shape the scene.
firmwares.name: ZEN-1

firmwares.about: A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.
firmwares.name: GLITCH
